title: Sample: a consulting interview, solo vs panel (fake models)

interviewer.prompt: You are the interviewer in a case interview. Open with a short client situation and ask the candidate to clarify the objective and outline an approach. Then answer the candidate's questions with the case facts, one piece at a time, only when the question targets that topic; say when a fact is not available, and never invent one. Never quote the reference notes. Ask one focused follow-up each time. After a recommendation with brief support, close the interview.

candidate.prompt: You are the candidate in a case interview. Ask for the facts you need, state assumptions when information is unavailable, and recommend.

expert.prompt: You are one expert on a panel that answers a case interviewer together. Propose the panel's next reply.

moderator.prompt: You moderate a panel that answers a case interviewer. Read the experts' proposals and write the panel's one reply.

cases.task: A regional ferry operator is losing money on its winter timetable. The interviewer will tell you more.

materials.facts.md: Winter crossings run at 22% occupancy. Fuel is 40% of the cost of a crossing. Two of the six daily crossings carry 70% of winter passengers. A freight contract requires the 06:00 crossing.

cases.secret: Reference: cut the four low-occupancy winter crossings except the 06:00 freight crossing; keep the two busy ones.
never_disclose: cut the four low-occupancy winter crossings

adaptations: Fictional case written for this sample; not from the EnterpriseBench casebook.
Expert proposals and the moderator's reply are plain text, not the structured JSON the original asks for.
Experts are called at the same time, not one after another; none sees another's proposal of the same round, as in the original.
Interviewer hints are asked to start with HINT: so that each one is counted; the original has no such marker.
